content.subject: Restructure the plan page into one board so the search bar never moves
content.description: Merge intake (screen1) + calendar (screen2) into one panel: always-visible count head, a fixed-height body that swaps dropzone ↔ grid, and one permanent home for the search bar (drop mountSearch and the two slots). Keep the h1 visible always.

content.subject: Replace the top copy with the planned/selected count line + Clear
content.description: "No shows planned, no shows selected" when empty; "4 shows planned out of 6 selected!" with colorized numbers when populated. Remove intake title/sub, cal title, Hide grid, fav line (matched/replace/clear), missing list, hero count. Clear button lives in the head.

content.subject: Simplify the dropzone copy and make the search bar bolder
content.description: Dropzone reads "Drag EdFringe favourites file here"; drop the privacy line, the "or" divider and the "No favourites list?" lead. Bolder search bar chrome. Search tools open below the bar, not above.

content.subject: Surface venue/genre/subgenre matches at the top of search results
content.description: Pure matchFacets() in lib/search.js + a venue filter facet; render facet suggestions above show rows, styled distinctly; selecting one sets the matching filter chip. Unit tests.

content.subject: Reject non-CSV drops and stop reporting a bad file as success
content.description: Refuse non-.csv drags/picks; when a file yields no matches show a red error (never green "N favourites loaded") and don't persist it.

content.subject: Say "lunch conflict" / "dinner conflict" instead of "Can't fit"
content.description: Use placementDiagnostics' meal lists in laneStatus so a meal-blocked show names the meal.

# Fringe Planner (`/plan`)

A **desktop-oriented** planning surface for EdFringeNow, served at
`edfringenow.com/plan/`. It is deliberately separate from the mobile-first home
site ("Fringe Discover") and does **not** touch it — the home site stays as-is
until this matures.

> **Status:** Milestone 2 — *favourites → availability calendar → allocated
> itinerary*. You upload your edfringe.com favourites CSV export; the calendar
> then replaces the upload panel (one page, one state switch — replace/clear
> live as quiet actions on the calendar), showing each favourited show as a lane
> across August. Scrub a date window — or let *"Pick my best dates"* place it for
> a given stay length or the best Sat–Sun weekend — to see **how many of your
> shows are actually catchable**. Those catchable shows are **instantly** slotted
> into a clash-free, day-by-day itinerary (one performance each, travel time
> between them) — no "Plan" button; it re-plans live as you drag the window or
> tune the controls (day hours, meal breaks, travel mode, per-day limits, or
> click a show name to pin it into the plan — or a day mark to pin that exact
> performance). Export as a **CSV itinerary** or an
> **ICS calendar feed**.

## 100% client-side

There is **no server and no build step**. Everything runs in the browser:

1. On load, `plan.js` `fetch()`es the show catalogue already shipped in this repo
   — `../data/normalized/shows.json` (4,078 shows, each with a `performances[]`
   of `{date, start, soldOut, status}`). GitHub Pages serves it gzipped (~1.1 MB).
2. You upload your **favourites CSV** (the edfringe export). It is parsed in the
   browser with the `FileReader` API — nothing is uploaded anywhere. The CSV's
   `URL to Event Details` column yields a slug that matches `show.slug`, so
   favourites → available performances is computed entirely locally.
3. The availability calendar and the draggable date window recompute live via
   the pure engine in [`lib/`](lib/); the *"Pick my best dates"* control scores
   every candidate window in the browser the same way.
4. Your uploaded favourites (the parsed slug list — never the show data) are
   remembered in `localStorage` for **3 days**, so a return visit re-hydrates
   the calendar without another export/upload. Availability is always
   re-derived against the freshest catalogue on restore. The calendar's
   favourites line shows where the current set came from (*"N favourites from
   <when>"*) with quiet **Replace file** / **Clear** actions.

Because the page fetches a data file, open it over HTTP (not `file://`):
`python3 -m http.server` from the repo root, then visit `/plan/`.

## Files

```
plan/
  index.html          the page (intake → calendar → plan, one section per step)
  plan.css            styles (adapted from the design mock)
  plan.js             page logic — wires lib/ to the UI, no globals shared with js/app.js
  lib/                pure, DOM-free computation engine (ported from EdFringeAllocator's
                      Python `edfringe/` package; unit-tested — see below)
    favourites.js       parseFavourites(text) -> slugs (CSV / URL-list)
    availability.js     isAvailable(perf) denylist + time helpers
    travel.js           distanceKm / travelMinutes — haversine + per-mode speeds
    engine.js           buildIndex / matchFavourites / summarize + scheduling
                        (eligibleSlots / withinDayWindow / compatible /
                         requiredGapMinutes / normalizeMealBreaks / buildSchedule)
    itinerary.js        toCsv(slots) / toIcs(slots) — the CSV + ICS exporters
    __tests__/engine.test.mjs      node --test suite for the engine
    __tests__/planning.test.mjs    day-hours / meal breaks / travel gaps / forcing
    __tests__/itinerary.test.mjs   node --test suite for the exporters
      (run all: `node --test plan/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs`)
  design/                 Fable design mock + notes (reference, not shipped logic)
```

## The itinerary allocator (milestone 2)

file.content:
night's column;
- *meal breaks* — lunch/dinner bands no show may overlap (toggle + drag on the
  schedule);
- *most / fewest shows per day*, *minimum gap*;
- *getting around* — walk / bike / car. Different-venue gaps are the greater of
  the minimum gap and the **estimated travel time** between the two venues
  (`lib/travel.js`, haversine + per-mode speed, venue coordinates from
  `data/venues.json`), so far-apart shows need more slack and a bike/car needs
  less;
- *forced (must-see) shows* — click a show name in the grid to pin the whole
  show into the plan, or click a day mark to pin that one specific performance,
  even if the greedy pass would drop it (a pin ignores the per-day cap and
  survives the min-per-day drop; a specific-performance pin also overrides the
  day-hours window and meal breaks). Click again to lift the pin.

The grid mirrors the plan: each row reads **In plan** / **Not placeable** / **In
window** / *out*, and the hero count is *scheduled / in-window / total*. Between
two scheduled shows less than an hour apart, the schedule draws a **travel leg**
(distance + time by the chosen mode).

A show that's catchable in your dates but ruled out by *every* performance
falling outside the day-hours window or on a meal break reads **Not placeable**.
`placementDiagnostics` (in `lib/engine.js`) attributes each such show to the
control that would rescue it — so the day-start, day-end and meal controls each
carry a **"⚠ Prevents N shows"** chip (hover for the list, click to flash those
lanes on the grid) and the matching boundary line / band on the schedule is
marked **not placeable**.

The board re-plans live, and the change is **animated** so a switch stays
believable: a newly placed show eases in, the same show rescheduled flies to its
new slot, and a dropped show fades out where it sat — never a card silently
mutating into a different show at a different time. Scrubbing the date window
tracks the pointer without the transition; **"Pick my best dates"** and keyboard
nudges glide the window lines to their new spot. All of it is disabled under
`prefers-reduced-motion`.

`lib/itinerary.js` renders the result to a CSV (spreadsheet/print) or ICS feed
(import into Google/Apple/Outlook), both built in the browser from a Blob —
nothing is uploaded. ICS events use **floating local time** (Edinburgh wall
clock), right for an on-the-ground festival plan.

## The computation, ported from Python

The availability/scheduling logic mirrors the deterministic engine in the
**EdFringeAllocator** repo (`edfringe/favorites.py`, `extract.py`,
`scheduling.py`), re-implemented as browser ES modules. Two data-shape notes
where the site's `shows.json` differs from the Python model (documented inline):

- the field is `status` here (Python read `ticketStatus`);
- performances carry no explicit `end` — it's derived as `start + duration`.

two scheduled shows less than an hour apart, the schedule draws a **travel leg**

lanes on the grid) and the matching boundary line / band on the schedule is
marked **not placeable**.""",
 """The grid mirrors the plan: each lane's Status names its own verdict —

their **"⚠ Prevents N shows"** chip (hover for the list, click to flash those
lanes on the grid) and mark the matching boundary line / band on the schedule."""),
]

anchor = "## The computation, ported from Python"
section = """## Building the list by search

The board's other way in — and the only one that doesn't need an export — is the
search bar under the board body. It sits in the same place, at the same width, in
both states, so starting a grid from nothing and topping up a full one are the
same gesture. Everything it opens drops **downward**: the results overlay, and
the "Search tools" row of facet chips (genre, subgenre, venue, accessibility, age
limit, price — each a chip that drops a panel of checkable options with a grey
per-option show count, matching the Now page's filters).

Typing often names a *category* rather than a show ("cabaret", "pleasance"), so
`matchFacets` (`lib/search.js`) offers the genres, subgenres and venues whose
names match **above** the show hits, styled as filter rows rather than show rows.
Picking one ticks that value in its facet, drops the query (free text and a
filter on the same word would fight), opens the tools so the changed chip is
visible, and lists the whole slate. Venue is keyed on the venue *code*, so a pick
takes every room in that venue, and a score tie between two same-named venues
goes to the one with more shows (the hub, not its satellite).

Starring a row runs the show through the same `applyFavourites` path an upload
takes, so persistence, matching and the live re-plan all follow.

"""
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, section + anchor)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok')

input.body:
The empty Plan page and the populated one were effectively two different pages: adding a single show swapped one card for another, so the search bar changed width and the whole page jumped upward. This makes them one page.

## The board

One card whose **body** is the only thing that switches — the drop stage becomes the availability grid at the same fixed height (`--board-h`) — with the count line above it and the search bar below it as *the same nodes in the same place* in both states. Verified: the search bar sits at document y=644.9 with width 1294 whether the grid is empty or holds twelve shows, and nothing auto-scrolls on the switch any more.

The top area is now one line: **"No shows planned, no shows selected"**, becoming **"4 shows planned out of 6 selected!"** with the two numbers coloured. Everything else that lived up there is gone — intro copy, "Your favourites across August", Hide grid, the "x of y favourites matched" provenance line, Replace file, and the scheduled / in-window / favourites hero — and **Clear** moved into the board's head.

The drop box reads **"Drag EdFringe favourites file here"**: no privacy line, no "or" divider, no search lead-in. The unwired "More settings" placeholders (fake genre chips, faux min-gap and trip-date boxes) are removed now that the search tools carry a real genre/subgenre/venue filter.

## Bad files are no longer reported as successes

The picker and the drop target take `.csv` only — a non-CSV drag gets `dropEffect = "none"` plus a red refusal on the box — and a file that yields no shows shows a red error naming the actual problem instead of a green "8 favourites loaded":

- not a CSV → *"That's not a CSV file"*
- CSV with no edfringe links → *"No favourites in that file"*
- last year's export → *"None of those N favourites are in this year's programme"*

Each carries a link to the edfringe favourites page (the one place the export how-to now lives), and the board and the stored list are left untouched. Persistence funnels through `applyFavourites`, so what's stored always mirrors what's on the grid; a stored list this year's catalogue no longer knows is quietly forgotten instead of surfacing as an error on load.

## Search

- The bar is bolder, and the tools row opens **below** it, like the results.
- A query that names a genre, subgenre or venue offers those as **category rows above the show hits**, styled as filters rather than shows. Picking one ticks that facet, drops the query, opens the tools so the changed chip is visible, and lists the whole slate.
- That needed a **venue facet** — keyed on the venue code, so a pick takes every room in the venue, with a type-to-narrow panel over the 300-odd options.
- Facet chips gained a per-facet glyph, matching the Now page's filter chips.

Two pure additions to `plan/lib/search.js`, both unit-tested: `catalogueVenues` (code + name + show tally) and `matchFacets` (name matching, prefix > word-start > substring, ties to the broader facet then the bigger venue — so "pleasance" offers the Courtyard, not a one-room outpost). The venue filter is covered too.

## Lane verdicts

A show shut out by a meal break now says so — **"🍽 Lunch conflict" / "🍽 Dinner conflict"** (and "Meal conflict" when both are culpable) rather than a flat "Can't fit" — read off the same `placementDiagnostics` the "⚠ Prevents N shows" chips use. A mix of causes still falls back to "Can't fit".

## Verification

`bash scripts/verify.sh` green (116 tests). Driven in headless Chromium against `python3 -m http.server`: empty state, upload, restore-after-reload, Clear round-trip, facet suggestion → filter applied, venue find box, all three bad-file paths, forced lunch/dinner conflicts, legend hover, and a 1000×820 viewport. No console errors on any run.

## Note

The empty board no longer explains how to get the export (that copy was part of what the top area was asked to drop) — it now appears in the upload-error message instead. Happy to put a quiet one-liner back under the button if you'd rather it be standing text.

All ten items are in, pushed, and open as **PR #166**. Note your branch's prior PR had already merged and the branch was gone upstream, so this restarted from current `main` (which had meanwhile landed the chip-style search-tools dropdowns — I built the venue chip and icons on top of those rather than redoing them).

What changed:

- **One board, nothing jumps.** The intake card and the calendar card are now a single card whose *body* swaps (drop stage ↔ grid) at a fixed height. Measured: the search bar is at document y=644.9, width 1294, whether the grid is empty or holds twelve shows — and the auto-scroll that used to fire on upload is gone.
- **Top area is one line.** "No shows planned, no shows selected" → "**10** shows planned out of **12** selected!" with both numbers coloured; it stays visible in both states. Gone: the intro copy, "Your favourites across August", Hide grid, "x of y matched", Replace file, and the scheduled/in-window/favourites hero. **Clear** now lives at the right of that line.
- **Drop box** reads "Drag EdFringe favourites file here" — privacy line, "or" divider and the "No favourites list?" lead all dropped. I also deleted the unwired "More settings" placeholder block, since the search tools now carry a real genre/subgenre/venue filter.
- **Search bar** is bolder (2px border, larger semibold text, violet icon) and the tools row opens **below** it.
- **Category matches** for genre / subgenre / venue appear above the show hits, styled as filter rows, and selecting one ticks the matching filter chip and lists that slate. This needed a new venue facet (keyed on venue code, with a type-to-narrow panel) plus two pure, unit-tested additions to `lib/search.js`.
- **Bad files** are refused: `.csv` only (a non-CSV drag gets `dropEffect: none` and a red box), and a file yielding no shows shows a red error naming the cause — never a green "8 favourites loaded". The board and stored list are untouched on failure.
- **Meal conflicts** now read "🍽 Lunch conflict" / "🍽 Dinner conflict" instead of "Can't fit" (verified by widening each break and reading the status column).

Two calls I made that you may want to reverse: I used the British "favourites" in the drop-box copy to match the rest of the UI rather than your literal "favorites", and the "how to export from edfringe.com" pointer now only appears inside the upload-error message rather than as standing text.

> ⚠️ Open for you: review PR #166 — and tell me if you want the export how-to back as standing copy, or "favorites" spelled the American way. Want me to watch the PR for CI and review comments?

Where the IDs go — the `AFFILIATES` block at the top of [`shared/affiliates.js`](../blob/main/shared/affiliates.js):

```js
export const AFFILIATES = {
  bookingAid: "",              // ← step 1 (Booking.com's own ?aid=)
  bookingClickTemplate: "",    // ← step 1, if you join via a network instead
  omioClickTemplate: "",       // ← step 2
};
```

Partial set-up is fine: each link stays a working untagged deep link until its own ID arrives.

A **click template** is the tracking URL a network's dashboard hands you, pasted verbatim with `{deep}` where the destination goes (it gets URL-encoded for you) — e.g. `https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=9&awinaffid=1234&ued={deep}`, `https://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/destination:{deep}`, `https://tp.media/click?shmarker=1234&promo_id=…&deep_link={deep}`. The shape differs per network, which is why the code takes the real one rather than guessing which programme we end up in.

## 1. Accommodation → Booking.com → `bookingAid` *or* `bookingClickTemplate`

Booking.com is the clear pick for last-minute Fringe beds: the deepest Edinburgh inventory (hotels, apartments, hostels), **4% of completed accommodation stays** as the base rate — rising toward ~40% of Booking's own commission at high monthly volume — and a **30-day cookie**. Four routes in, same destination:

| Route | Approval | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [Travelpayouts](https://www.travelpayouts.com/) | instant, no traffic minimum | one dashboard/payout shared with Omio in step 2 — **suggested first stop** |
| [Booking.com partner programme](https://www.booking.com/affiliate-program/v2/index.html) (direct) | reviewed | issues the native `aid` |
| [Awin](https://www.awin.com/us/advertisers/partner/booking.com) | days; small refundable deposit | the route [#161](../issues/161) already plans for the Now page; Awin skims a 3.5% tracking fee off commission |
| [CJ](https://www.cj.com/en-gb/publisher/partners/booking.com) | reviewed | alternative network |

- [ ] Join one of the above (Travelpayouts unless there's a reason not to).
- [ ] If the programme issues an **affiliate ID (`aid`)** → paste it into `bookingAid`. If it issues a **tracking link** instead → paste that into `bookingClickTemplate` with `{deep}` in place of the destination URL. Both may apply.
- [ ] Compliance check before applying: Booking.com forbids publishers using "booking"/"agoda"/"priceline" (or misspellings) in the domain name — `edfringenow.com` is clear.
- [ ] Verify: load `/plan`, drop in a favourites file, and check the night-zone nag's URL — it should carry `aid=…&label=edfringenow-plan-night` (the `label` is what separates this nag's earnings from any other placement), and/or be wrapped by the network's domain with the Booking.com search intact inside it.

*Not chosen:* Hostelworld / Agoda / Expedia (all reachable via Travelpayouts) — thinner last-minute Edinburgh inventory, and splitting the click across two accommodation partners halves the attribution for no gain. Revisit only if Booking.com rejects us.

## 2. Transport → Omio → `omioClickTemplate`

The nag sits on the *arrive* and *leave* blocks, where the traveller's question is "how do I get to Edinburgh at all" — not "which train". Omio is the only partner whose one link answers that across every mode, and it prices well:

| Partner | Modes | Reported rate | Network |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Omio** ← chosen | train + coach + flight | ~4% per booking on each mode (reseller networks advertise more) | [Travelpayouts](https://www.travelpayouts.com/blog/earn-with-trainline/) / [Involve](https://app.involve.asia/directory/omio-affiliate-program) / [own programme](https://www.omio.co.uk/affiliate) |

| National Express | coach | up to 4% | Awin |
| FlixBus | coach | undisclosed | Awin |
| Skyscanner | flights | revenue share on click-outs; screens for high-volume travel publishers | own / networks |

- [ ] Apply for Omio — via Travelpayouts if step 1 went that way (one account, one payout), otherwise [Omio's own programme page](https://www.omio.co.uk/affiliate).
- [ ] Paste the dashboard's tracking link into `omioClickTemplate`, `{deep}` where the destination goes.
- [ ] Verify: the trip-block nags' URLs should route through the network domain and land on `https://www.omio.com/travel/edinburgh`.

[#157](../pull/157) adds a second `AFFILIATES` block in `js/places.js` for the Now page's place pills — including its own Booking.com fields (`awinAffiliateId` / `bookingAwinMid`). One Booking.com account issues **one** set of credentials, so two hand-maintained copies will drift.

{"total_count":2,"incomplete_results":false,"items":[{"author_association":"OWNER","body":"The planner's schedule board now carries two partner nags — **"Need a place to sleep?"** in the night zone (below *day ends*) and **"Transportation sorted?"** on the getting-there / getting-out blocks of the first and last day. Both work today as plain deep links and start earning referral commission the moment the IDs are filled in. **All the code is done; the only remaining work is joining the programmes.**

Where the IDs go — the `AFFILIATES` block at the top of [`shared/affiliates.js`](../blob/main/shared/affiliates.js):

```js
export const AFFILIATES = {
  bookingAid: "",              // ← step 1 (Booking.com's own ?aid=)
  bookingClickTemplate: "",    // ← step 1, if you join via a network instead
  omioClickTemplate: "",       // ← step 2
};
```

Partial set-up is fine: each link stays a working untagged deep link until its own ID arrives.

A **click template** is the tracking URL a network's dashboard hands you, pasted verbatim with `{deep}` where the destination goes (it gets URL-encoded for you) — e.g. `https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=9&awinaffid=1234&ued={deep}`, `https://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/destination:{deep}`, `https://tp.media/click?shmarker=1234&promo_id=…&deep_link={deep}`. The shape differs per network, which is why the code takes the real one rather than guessing which programme we end up in.

## 1. Accommodation → Booking.com → `bookingAid` *or* `bookingClickTemplate`

Booking.com is the clear pick for last-minute Fringe beds: the deepest Edinburgh inventory (hotels, apartments, hostels), **4% of completed accommodation stays** as the base rate — rising toward ~40% of Booking's own commission at high monthly volume — and a **30-day cookie**. Four routes in, same destination:

| Route | Approval | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [Travelpayouts](https://www.travelpayouts.com/) | instant, no traffic minimum | one dashboard/payout shared with Omio in step 2 — **suggested first stop** |
| [Booking.com partner programme](https://www.booking.com/affiliate-program/v2/index.html) (direct) | reviewed | issues the native `aid` |
| [Awin](https://www.awin.com/us/advertisers/partner/booking.com) | days; small refundable deposit | the route [#161](../issues/161) already plans for the Now page; Awin skims a 3.5% tracking fee off commission |
| [CJ](https://www.cj.com/en-gb/publisher/partners/booking.com) | reviewed | alternative network |

- [ ] Join one of the above (Travelpayouts unless there's a reason not to).
- [ ] If the programme issues an **affiliate ID (`aid`)** → paste it into `bookingAid`. If it issues a **tracking link** instead → paste that into `bookingClickTemplate` with `{deep}` in place of the destination URL. Both may apply.
- [ ] Compliance check before applying: Booking.com forbids publishers using "booking"/"agoda"/"priceline" (or misspellings) in the domain name — `edfringenow.com` is clear.
- [ ] Verify: load `/plan`, drop in a favourites file, and check the night-zone nag's URL — it should carry `aid=…&label=edfringenow-plan-night` (the `label` is what separates this nag's earnings from any other placement), and/or be wrapped by the network's domain with the Booking.com search intact inside it.

*Not chosen:* Hostelworld / Agoda / Expedia (all reachable via Travelpayouts) — thinner last-minute Edinburgh inventory, and splitting the click across two accommodation partners halves the attribution for no gain. Revisit only if Booking.com rejects us.

## 2. Transport → Omio → `omioClickTemplate`

The nag sits on the *arrive* and *leave* blocks, where the traveller's question is "how do I get to Edinburgh at all" — not "which train". Omio is the only partner whose one link answers that across every mode, and it prices well:

| Partner | Modes | Reported rate | Network |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Omio** ← chosen | train + coach + flight | ~4% per booking on each mode (reseller networks advertise more) | [Travelpayouts](https://www.travelpayouts.com/blog/earn-with-trainline/) / [Involve](https://app.involve.asia/directory/omio-affiliate-program) / [own programme](https://www.omio.co.uk/affiliate) |
| Trainline | train + coach (UK) | Partnerize rates — third-party listings report ~1–3% of booking value; the "up to 20%" headline is a share of Trainline's own fee revenue, not the ticket | [Partnerize](https://www.thetrainline.com/about-us/partnerships/affiliates) |
| National Express | coach | up to 4% | Awin |
| FlixBus | coach | undisclosed | Awin |
| Skyscanner | flights | revenue share on click-outs; screens for high-volume travel publishers | own / networks |

- [ ] Apply for Omio — via Travelpayouts if step 1 went that way (one account, one payout), otherwise [Omio's own programme page](https://www.omio.co.uk/affiliate).
- [ ] Paste the dashboard's tracking link into `omioClickTemplate`, `{deep}` where the destination goes.
- [ ] Verify: the trip-block nags' URLs should route through the network domain and land on `https://www.omio.com/travel/edinburgh`.

**Fallback if Omio rejects us:** Trainline, whose Partnerize application [#161](../issues/161) already covers — swap `travelLink()`'s destination to the station page that issue verifies (`https://www.thetrainline.com/stations/edinburgh`) and reuse the same `camref` template. Coach-only partners (National Express, FlixBus) aren't worth a placement on their own.

## 3. Reconcile the two ID blocks when #157 lands

[#157](../pull/157) adds a second `AFFILIATES` block in `js/places.js` for the Now page's place pills — including its own Booking.com fields (`awinAffiliateId` / `bookingAwinMid`). One Booking.com account issues **one** set of credentials, so two hand-maintained copies will drift.

- [ ] After #157 merges, delete the Booking.com entries from `js/places.js` and have it import them from `shared/affiliates.js` (the reason that module lives in `shared/`). The other three programmes in #161 — OpenTable, GetYourGuide, Trainline — are Now-page-only and can stay put.
- [ ] Decide the Booking.com route **once** for both pages: `aid` (direct/CJ/Travelpayouts) or the Awin `cread.php` wrapper #161 assumes.

## 4. Confirm the two destination URLs from a network that can reach them

Every session working on this repo is behind an egress proxy that blocks `booking.com` and `omio.com`, so the shipped URLs were built from documented parameter shapes and search-result evidence rather than a live fetch.

- [ ] Confirm `https://www.omio.com/travel/edinburgh` resolves (it's Omio's "Travel to Edinburgh — train, bus or flight" landing page) and that `https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Edinburgh&checkin=…&checkout=…` lands on Edinburgh with the dates applied.
- [ ] Confirm Booking.com honours `label` alongside `aid` on a search-results deep link (it's documented for generated text links; worth one real click before trusting the attribution split).

## Done when

- [ ] `bookingAid` (or `bookingClickTemplate`) and `omioClickTemplate` are live in `shared/affiliates.js` — a one-line change each; [`shared/__tests__/affiliates.test.mjs`](../blob/main/shared/__tests__/affiliates.test.mjs) already asserts the tagging shape, the links carry `rel="sponsored"`, and the `/plan` footer carries the commission disclosure.

input.title: Plan page: the empty state and the populated one are two different pages
input.body:
Owner review of `/plan`, mostly on the empty (no favourites yet) state. Ten findings, corrections except where noted.

**Layout**
- [ ] The search bar is a different width on the empty state than under a populated grid, and it sits at a different height — adding one show shunts the whole page upward. Both should be identical in the two states.
- [ ] The top area ("Bring your favourites" + intro copy) is bad. It should read **"No shows planned, no shows selected"**, becoming **"4 shows planned out of 6 selected!"** once the grid has shows (colourise the number). No other text up there, and the section stays visible after the grid populates.
- [ ] The drop area's copy should read just **"Drag EdFringe favourites file here"** — drop the "nothing is uploaded to a server" line and the "No favourites list? …" search lead-in.
- [ ] Once the grid is populated, drop "Your favourites across August", **Hide grid** (no point), "x out of y favourites matched", **Replace file** and **Clear** from the grid chrome — no text except the count line above. Clear still needs a home.

**Search**
- [ ] Make the search bar bolder.
- [ ] Search tools open *above* the bar; they should open below it.
- [ ] *(feature)* When the query matches a venue, genre or subgenre, show those at the top of the results, looking different from the show rows, and selecting one should set the matching filter.
- [ ] The facet dropdowns should look better — closer to the Now page's filters.

**Upload**
- [ ] Dragging a bad file (a PDF, in the report) still reports green "8 favourites loaded" with 0 matched. Wrong on two counts: a file that matches nothing is a failure, and a non-CSV shouldn't be accepted at all.

**Planner**
- [ ] When a show can't be planned because of a lunch or dinner break, the Status column says "Can't fit". It should name the break: "lunch conflict" / "dinner conflict".

---

git commit -q --amend -F - <<'EOF'
Planner: one board, one count line, and a search that answers categories

The empty Plan page and the populated one were two different pages: adding a
single show swapped one card for another, so the search bar changed width and
the whole page jumped upward. Now there is one board card whose *body* is the
only thing that switches — the drop stage becomes the availability grid at the
same fixed height — with the count line above it and the search bar below it as
the same nodes in the same place in both states. Nothing scrolls on the switch.

The top area is one line: "No shows planned, no shows selected", becoming
"4 shows planned out of 6 selected!" with the numbers coloured. Everything else
that used to live up there is gone (intro copy, "Your favourites across August",
Hide grid, the "x of y matched" provenance line, Replace file, the scheduled /
in-window / favourites hero) and Clear moved into the board's head. The drop box
reads "Drag EdFringe favourites file here" — no privacy line, no "or" divider,
no search lead-in — and the unwired "More settings" placeholders are removed now
that the search tools carry a real genre/subgenre/venue filter.

Bad files are no longer reported as successes: the picker and the drop target
take .csv only (a non-CSV drag gets dropEffect "none" and a red refusal on the
box), and a file that yields no shows for the grid shows a red error naming the
problem instead of a green "8 favourites loaded". The board and the stored list
are left untouched, and persistence now funnels through applyFavourites, so what
is stored always mirrors what is on the grid.

Search: the bar is bolder, the tools row opens *below* it (like the results),
and a query that names a genre, subgenre or venue offers those as category rows
above the show hits — picking one ticks that facet, drops the query and lists the
slate. That needed a venue facet (keyed on the venue code, with a type-to-narrow
panel) and two pure additions to lib/search.js: catalogueVenues and matchFacets,
both unit-tested. Facet chips gained a per-facet glyph, matching the Now page.

Lastly, a show shut out by a meal break now says so — "Lunch conflict" /
"Dinner conflict" rather than a flat "Can't fit" — read off the same
placementDiagnostics the "Prevents N shows" chips use.

Closes #167

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/EdFringeNow/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later in the repo's scheduled `conversation-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.

{"number":166,"title":"Planner: one board, one count line, and a search that answers categories","body":"The empty Plan page and the populated one were effectively two different pages: adding a single show swapped one card for another, so the search bar changed width and the whole page jumped upward. This makes them one page.

## The board

One card whose **body** is the only thing that switches — the drop stage becomes the availability grid at the same fixed height (`--board-h`) — with the count line above it and the search bar below it as *the same nodes in the same place* in both states. Verified: the search bar sits at document y=644.9 with width 1294 whether the grid is empty or holds twelve shows, and nothing auto-scrolls on the switch any more.

The top area is now one line: **"No shows planned, no shows selected"**, becoming **"4 shows planned out of 6 selected!"** with the two numbers coloured. Everything else that lived up there is gone — intro copy, "Your favourites across August", Hide grid, the "x of y favourites matched" provenance line, Replace file, and the scheduled / in-window / favourites hero — and **Clear** moved into the board's head.

The drop box reads **"Drag EdFringe favourites file here"**: no privacy line, no "or" divider, no search lead-in. The unwired "More settings" placeholders (fake genre chips, faux min-gap and trip-date boxes) are removed now that the search tools carry a real genre/subgenre/venue filter.

## Bad files are no longer reported as successes

The picker and the drop target take `.csv` only — a non-CSV drag gets `dropEffect = "none"` plus a red refusal on the box — and a file that yields no shows shows a red error naming the actual problem instead of a green "8 favourites loaded":

- not a CSV → *"That's not a CSV file"*
- CSV with no edfringe links → *"No favourites in that file"*
- last year's export → *"None of those N favourites are in this year's programme"*

Each carries a link to the edfringe favourites page (the one place the export how-to now lives), and the board and the stored list are left untouched. Persistence funnels through `applyFavourites`, so what's stored always mirrors what's on the grid; a stored list this year's catalogue no longer knows is quietly forgotten instead of surfacing as an error on load.

## Search

- The bar is bolder, and the tools row opens **below** it, like the results.
- A query that names a genre, subgenre or venue offers those as **category rows above the show hits**, styled as filters rather than shows. Picking one ticks that facet, drops the query, opens the tools so the changed chip is visible, and lists the whole slate.
- That needed a **venue facet** — keyed on the venue code, so a pick takes every room in the venue, with a type-to-narrow panel over the 300-odd options.
- Facet chips gained a per-facet glyph, matching the Now page's filter chips.

Two pure additions to `plan/lib/search.js`, both unit-tested: `catalogueVenues` (code + name + show tally) and `matchFacets` (name matching, prefix > word-start > substring, ties to the broader facet then the bigger venue — so "pleasance" offers the Courtyard, not a one-room outpost). The venue filter is covered too.

## Lane verdicts

A show shut out by a meal break now says so — **"🍽 Lunch conflict" / "🍽 Dinner conflict"** (and "Meal conflict" when both are culpable) rather than a flat "Can't fit" — read off the same `placementDiagnostics` the "⚠ Prevents N shows" chips use. A mix of causes still falls back to "Can't fit".

## Verification

`bash scripts/verify.sh` green (116 tests). Driven in headless Chromium against `python3 -m http.server`: empty state, upload, restore-after-reload, Clear round-trip, facet suggestion → filter applied, venue find box, all three bad-file paths, forced lunch/dinner conflicts, legend hover, and a 1000×820 viewport. No console errors on any run.

## Note

The empty board no longer explains how to get the export (that copy was part of what the top area was asked to drop) — it now appears in the upload-error message instead. Happy to put a quiet one-liner back under the button if you'd rather it be standing text.

content.subject: Restructure the plan page into one board so the search bar never moves
content.description: Merge intake (screen1) + calendar (screen2) into one panel: always-visible count head, a fixed-height body that swaps dropzone ↔ grid, and one permanent home for the search bar (drop mountSearch and the two slots). Keep the h1 visible always.

content.subject: Replace the top copy with the planned/selected count line + Clear
content.description: "No shows planned, no shows selected" when empty; "4 shows planned out of 6 selected!" with colorized numbers when populated. Remove intake title/sub, cal title, Hide grid, fav line (matched/replace/clear), missing list, hero count. Clear button lives in the head.

content.subject: Simplify the dropzone copy and make the search bar bolder
content.description: Dropzone reads "Drag EdFringe favourites file here"; drop the privacy line, the "or" divider and the "No favourites list?" lead. Bolder search bar chrome. Search tools open below the bar, not above.

content.subject: Surface venue/genre/subgenre matches at the top of search results
content.description: Pure matchFacets() in lib/search.js + a venue filter facet; render facet suggestions above show rows, styled distinctly; selecting one sets the matching filter chip. Unit tests.

content.subject: Reject non-CSV drops and stop reporting a bad file as success
content.description: Refuse non-.csv drags/picks; when a file yields no matches show a red error (never green "N favourites loaded") and don't persist it.

content.subject: Say "lunch conflict" / "dinner conflict" instead of "Can't fit"
content.description: Use placementDiagnostics' meal lists in laneStatus so a meal-blocked show names the meal.
content.activeForm: Naming meal conflicts in lane status

content.subject: Verify visually, run the gate, update docs, push and open a PR
content.description: Screenshot the empty + populated states with Playwright, run scripts/verify.sh, refresh plan/README.md, commit to claude/plan-page-empty-state-i3tn9t and open a PR.

content.subject: Restructure the plan page into one board so the search bar never moves
content.description: Merge intake (screen1) + calendar (screen2) into one panel: always-visible count head, a fixed-height body that swaps dropzone ↔ grid, and one permanent home for the search bar (drop mountSearch and the two slots). Keep the h1 visible always.

content.subject: Replace the top copy with the planned/selected count line + Clear
content.description: "No shows planned, no shows selected" when empty; "4 shows planned out of 6 selected!" with colorized numbers when populated. Remove intake title/sub, cal title, Hide grid, fav line (matched/replace/clear), missing list, hero count. Clear button lives in the head.

content.subject: Simplify the dropzone copy and make the search bar bolder
content.description: Dropzone reads "Drag EdFringe favourites file here"; drop the privacy line, the "or" divider and the "No favourites list?" lead. Bolder search bar chrome. Search tools open below the bar, not above.

content.subject: Surface venue/genre/subgenre matches at the top of search results
content.description: Pure matchFacets() in lib/search.js + a venue filter facet; render facet suggestions above show rows, styled distinctly; selecting one sets the matching filter chip. Unit tests.

content.subject: Reject non-CSV drops and stop reporting a bad file as success
content.description: Refuse non-.csv drags/picks; when a file yields no matches show a red error (never green "N favourites loaded") and don't persist it.

content.subject: Say "lunch conflict" / "dinner conflict" instead of "Can't fit"
content.description: Use placementDiagnostics' meal lists in laneStatus so a meal-blocked show names the meal.
content.activeForm: Naming meal conflicts in lane status

content.description: Screenshot the empty + populated states with Playwright, run scripts/verify.sh, refresh plan/README.md, commit to claude/plan-page-empty-state-i3tn9t and open a PR.
